newsitem.title: MEXICO: Peace talks with Mexican rebels hit roadblock.
newsitem.headline: Peace talks with Mexican rebels hit roadblock.
newsitem.dateline: SAN CRISTOBAL DE LAS CASAS, Mexico 1997-02-14

text.p: Long-running talks aimed at securing peace between Zapatista rebels and the Mexican government ran into another roadblock on Friday amid bickering between the two sides.

A commission set up to verify various accords already reached between the government and the mainly Mayan rebels called off a key meeting on Friday after members of the Zapatista National Liberation Army (EZLN) failed to show up, government officials said in a statement.

The failure of the EZLN members to arrive for the meeting of the group charged with monitoring the fragile accords meant "we did not consider it appropriate to take part (in the meeting)," the Commission for Verificiation (COSEVE) said.

The Zapatista rebels, who led a brief and violent uprising in the southern state of Chiapas starting in 1994, said they could not leave their jungle strongholds because of an increased military presence.
The rebels and the federal government have been engaged in an increasingly strident war of words over how the peace talks should progress since they broke off about five months ago.
